analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) FX Trader Call Today, 2) Fed Call Change, 3) BRL Update, 4) Latest on El Nino and TTF and 5) Equities Update (11 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS now expects a second 25bp Fed hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike in March 2027. A January hike is possible, but March is judged more likely.

GS expects November and December inflation reports to be softer, then larger start-of-year price increases to lift January inflation. It expects inflation to be meaningfully lower by end-2027 as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressures fade.

GS expects most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. A firmer January inflation report would make the hike the path of least resistance even if the energy shock appears over.
GS left its terminal fed funds forecast unchanged at 3.25-3.5%, but now expects cuts to begin in December 2027 (previously September 2027), followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.
October core CPI rose 0.30%, above expectations, on firmness across a broad set of categories including shelter, medical services and rebounding motor vehicle insurance.
From the CPI details GS estimates October core PCE at +0.35% m/m (vs its 0.23% expectation before CPI), or +3.30% y/y. It estimates headline PCE at +0.36% m/m and +3.87% y/y.

Copom minutes were broadly neutral with a dovish tilt. The central bank attributes the worse inflation path mainly to first-round supply shocks it does not plan to react to, which suggests a high bar for near-term hikes. GS expects Copom to hold until at least 2Q27.

USDBRL returned to post-election highs on a stronger USD, lower oil, unclear fiscal measures and dovish BCB communication. GS flags the risk that high rates become unmanageable without a clearer fiscal anchor, and the market is now pricing hikes, so an on-hold stance may not support BRL near term.
Press reports of a possible fiscal adjustment (excluding certain revenues from the spending-growth calculation) fall short of spending cuts but may support BRL after the selloff.

GS FX trading says USDBRL broke 5.53, tested YTD highs and traded through 5.60 after the stronger CPI, with CTA USD buying. Offshore corporate USD supply appeared near 5.60. The desk sees around 5.60 as an OK sell, with resistance near 5.61.
BRL DIs closed sideways. The curve widened about 20bps from the day lows after the US CPI risk-off, and the Jan29 DI held near 14.70.

GS commodities research says the Super El Nino is confirmed by NOAA, but ECMWF models still show a roughly average Nov-Mar winter for NW Europe. It expects TTF to respond mainly to Middle East escalation/de-escalation headlines and short-run weather models.
GS's 1Q27 TTF forecast is 74 EUR/MWh, built from 44 EUR fair value plus a 26/4 EUR supply/weather risk premium. Mideast LNG supply has averaged above 40% of pre-war levels over the past week.

GS European gas trading cites reports of Hormuz negotiations, an unusually early sudden stratospheric warming event that could bring cold weather in early/mid December, and talk of reopening Russian gas flows. Gas has sold off as risk positions were unwound.

GS equity flow desk says SPX barely fell on the hot CPI and futures were recovering. VIX briefly traded into the 20s but closed below 20, which it reads as positioning supporting the tape more than macro undermines it.

The desk calls positioning a tailwind and the Fed a headwind. Gross exposure is cut, net exposure is historically low and appetite to add risk has diminished. It expects volatility premium to decay absent fresh negative news.

Rates are a headwind but not yet flashing red. Yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem, high yield spreads are chopping sideways, and the desk watches whether the Fed is reacting to energy effects already past.
Neocloud commentary was broadly supportive, with data centre capacity the main bottleneck and compute utilization elevated. US bond market was closed for Veterans Day while equities were open.

risk_factors: Higher oil leading to stickier inflation and a more hawkish Fed.
High yield credit spreads, which the desk calls the one to watch.
Brazil fiscal anchor risk and high real rates becoming unmanageable.
Early sudden stratospheric warming bringing cold weather to Europe and Asia in December.
Middle East re-escalation affecting LNG supply.
vol_and_positioning: VIX briefly traded into the 20s on the hot CPI but finished below 20.
GS flow desk says gross exposure has been cut, net exposure is historically low and investors are heavily hedged.
Volatility remains elevated relative to price action, and the premium should decay absent new negative information.
CTA names were USD buyers in USDBRL, adding momentum after the CPI.
geopolitical: Reports of negotiations on opening the Strait of Hormuz, including changes in Iranian stance on nuclear issues and a possible US release of frozen assets.
Mentions of reopening Russian gas flows to Europe.
Re-escalation/de-escalation headlines in the Middle East are cited as a main driver of TTF.
Brazil: reports that Fontelles would take the finance minister job if Lula invites him, and a possible fiscal adjustment in a complementary bill.

tension_points.bull_case: Cut gross exposure, historically low net exposure and heavy hedging mean positioning supports the tape, and the volatility premium should decay absent new negative information.
tension_points.bear_case: Rates are a headwind, higher oil means stickier inflation and a more hawkish Fed, and high yield credit is the one to watch.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields needing another leg higher, or fresh negative information that keeps the volatility premium from decaying.
